frame: Equatorial J2000, Sol at origin, +X towards RA 0h, +Z towards the north celestial pole
sources: data/nebulae_curated.csv (well-known nebulae; distance references per entry)
González-Santamaría et al. 2021, A&A 656, A51: planetary nebulae with Gaia EDR3 central-star distances
Zucker et al. 2020, A&A 633, A51: Gaia DR2 distances to molecular clouds (one puff per sightline)
puffs_format: [x, y, z, radius] in parsecs, equatorial J2000

nebulae.name: Orion Nebula
nebulae.notes: Nearest massive star-forming region; lit by the Trapezium cluster.

nebulae.name: De Mairan's Nebula
nebulae.notes: H II region around NU Ori; part of the Orion Nebula complex.

nebulae.name: Flame Nebula
nebulae.notes: Ionised by Alnitak's neighbourhood; embedded young cluster.

nebulae.name: Horsehead Nebula
nebulae.notes: Dark pillar silhouetted against the emission nebula IC 434.

nebulae.name: M78
nebulae.notes: Brightest reflection nebula in the sky.

nebulae.name: NGC 1999
nebulae.notes: Lit by the young star V380 Ori.

nebulae.name: Barnard's Loop
nebulae.notes: Huge arc of ionised gas blown out by the Orion OB1 association.

nebulae.name: Lambda Orionis Ring
nebulae.notes: Ring of gas and dust around the Lambda Ori cluster.

nebulae.name: Gum Nebula
nebulae.notes: Ancient supernova remnant / H II region about 36° across, one of the largest nebulae in the sky.

nebulae.name: Trifid Nebula
nebulae.notes: Emission + reflection + dark lanes in one object.

nebulae.name: Eagle Nebula
nebulae.notes: Home of the Pillars of Creation.

nebulae.name: Rosette Nebula
nebulae.notes: Shell carved by the cluster NGC 2244.

nebulae.name: Hubble's Variable Nebula
nebulae.notes: Fan-shaped nebula lit by R Monocerotis; varies over weeks.

nebulae.name: Thor's Helmet
nebulae.notes: Wind-blown bubble around the Wolf-Rayet star WR 7.

nebulae.name: Pelican Nebula
nebulae.notes: Part of the same H II region as the North America Nebula.

nebulae.name: Crescent Nebula
nebulae.notes: Wind-blown shell around the Wolf-Rayet star WR 136.

nebulae.name: Bubble Nebula
nebulae.notes: Bubble blown by the O star BD+60° 2522.

nebulae.name: Ghost of Cassiopeia
nebulae.notes: Lit and eroded by Gamma Cassiopeiae.

nebulae.name: California Nebula
nebulae.notes: Ionised by the runaway O star Xi Persei.

nebulae.name: NGC 1333
nebulae.notes: Young embedded cluster in the Perseus molecular cloud.

nebulae.name: Flaming Star Nebula
nebulae.notes: Lit by the runaway star AE Aurigae.

nebulae.name: Pleiades Nebula
nebulae.notes: Dust cloud the Pleiades are passing through (Merope Nebula).

nebulae.name: Rho Ophiuchi Nebula
nebulae.notes: Closest star-forming region to the Sun with multicoloured nebulosity.

nebulae.name: Chamaeleon Nebula
nebulae.notes: Brightest nebula of the Chamaeleon I cloud.

nebulae.name: Carina Nebula
nebulae.notes: Home of Eta Carinae; one of the brightest H II regions in the Galaxy.

nebulae.name: Helix Nebula
nebulae.notes: One of the closest bright planetary nebulae.

nebulae.name: Bug Nebula
nebulae.notes: Butterfly-shaped; one of the hottest known central stars.

nebulae.name: Sh2-216
nebulae.notes: Nearest known planetary nebula; very old and faint.

nebulae.name: Crab Nebula
nebulae.notes: Remnant of the supernova of 1054 AD, powered by the Crab pulsar.

nebulae.name: Veil Nebula / Cygnus Loop
nebulae.notes: Supernova remnant about 10–20 thousand years old.

nebulae.name: Vela Supernova Remnant
nebulae.notes: About 11,000 years old; contains the Vela pulsar.

nebulae.name: Cassiopeia A
nebulae.notes: Youngest known Galactic core-collapse remnant (about 1680 AD).

nebulae.name: Tycho's Supernova Remnant
nebulae.notes: Remnant of the Type Ia supernova seen by Tycho Brahe in 1572.

nebulae.name: Kepler's Supernova Remnant
nebulae.notes: Last supernova seen in the Milky Way with the naked eye (1604).

nebulae.name: Manatee Nebula
nebulae.notes: Supernova remnant distorted by the jets of the microquasar SS 433.

nebulae.name: Coalsack Nebula
nebulae.notes: The most prominent dark nebula visible to the naked eye.

nebulae.name: Barnard 68
nebulae.notes: Isolated dense core (Bok globule) on the verge of collapse.

nebulae.name: Dark Doodad
nebulae.notes: Long thin filament of dust in Musca.
